{{Quote|She died in my arms. You should've seen what those filth did to her.|Saylew|<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />}}
'''Saylew''' was a [[Rutian/Legends|Rutian]] [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who was a member of the religious group known as the [[Pilgrims]] during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. Along with his [[Saylew's wife|wife]], Saylew settled in [[Kalikori village]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tython/Legends|Tython]]. In [[3643 BBY]], during a [[Flesh Raider uprising|conflict]] with Tython's native [[Flesh Raider]]s, Saylew's [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] was [[Death/Legends|killed]] in an [[Attack on Kalikori village|attack]] on the [[City/Legends|village]], and an enraged Saylew sought vengeance on the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] for not helping the villagers&mdash;going so far as to betray the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to the Flesh Raiders' leader, the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Bengel Morr]]. However, the villagers' betrayal was ultimately for naught, as Morr was defeated.

==Biography==
A [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], Saylew [[Marriage/Legends|married]] a [[Saylew's wife|female]] of his [[Species/Legends|species]], and both were members of the religious group known as the [[Pilgrims]] during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. Along with the other Pilgrims, they settled on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], where they constructed [[Kalikori village]] despite the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate's]] refusal of settlement rights, and they struggled to survive in the face of attacks by the hostile native [[Flesh Raider]]s without aid from the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. The [[Flesh Raider uprising|conflict]] with the Flesh Raiders reached its peak<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> in [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Time">{{TOR_dates|1}}</ref> when the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] finally reached out to the villagers in an attempt to combat the Flesh Raider threat. However, an [[Attack on Kalikori village|attack]] on the [[City/Legends|village]] saw Saylew's wife [[Death/Legends|killed]] by the Flesh Raiders, leaving Saylew mad with grief and anger.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

He interrupted a meeting between [[Scout Chief]] [[Moorint]]; the village [[Matriarch/Legends|matriarch's]] daughter, [[Ranna Tao'Ven]]; and [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Orgus Din]] and demanded retribution for the loss of his wife and vengeance upon her killers. Din cautioned Saylew on his feelings of vengeance, angering Saylew further, but his ranting was interrupted by the arrival of [[Hero of Tython|Din's Padawan]], who had just retrieved a cache of Flesh Raider weapons. Still irate, Saylew stormed out of the building.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

Not long afterward, the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Bengel Morr]]&mdash;who was responsible for marshaling the Flesh Raiders into an [[Army/Legends|army]]&mdash;approached the villagers with an offer: In return for helping him capture his former Master, Orgus Din, the Dark Jedi would spare Kalikori from further attacks. The villagers agreed and sent out a false [[Distress signal/Legends|distress signal]], luring Din back to the village, where Morr's Flesh Raiders subdued and captured the Jedi Master. However, Morr soon contacted the village again and changed their deal, demanding the life of Din's [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] as well. Along with Moorint and a villager named [[Eseni]], Saylew headed to the matriarch's building, where the recently arrived Padawan was speaking with Tao'Ven and the [[T7-series astromech droid|astromech droid]] [[T7-O1]].<ref name="Dark Temptations">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Dark Temptations|Tython}}</ref>

{{GameLS}}
[[File:Betrayal.png|thumb|right|220px|The villagers attempt to kill the Padawan.]]
While the Jedi was talking, Moorint shot the Padawan with a [[Dart/Legends|dart]] coated with a sedative and painkiller, and Saylew shot T7-O1 with an [[Ion blaster/Legends|ion blaster]]. However, Tao'Ven was outraged by their actions and leaped to the Jedi's defense, and she began to argue with the villagers, refusing to let them kill the Padawan as the Jedi struggled to remain conscious. The Padawan soon recovered and questioned the villagers' intentions, and Moorint explained that Morr was demanding the Jedi's life. Before the villagers could attack, the Padawan reached out with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and [[Mind trick/Legends|convinced]] the trio to leave the building peacefully.<ref name="Dark Temptations" /> Despite their failure to comply with Moorint's demands, the villagers were spared from Morr's wrath when Din's apprentice [[Battle of the Forge|defeated]] the Dark Jedi and rescued Din.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Weapon of the Jedi|Tython}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

==Personality and traits==
A Twi'lek of the [[Rutian/Legends|Rutian]] subspecies, Saylew had [[Color/Legends|blue]] skin and green [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. He loved his wife dearly&mdash;love that turned to hatred of the Flesh Raiders when she was taken from him. Saylew was more than willing to betray and kill the Jedi in hopes of saving himself and the village, and his mind was weak enough for him to fall prey to mind tricks.<ref name="Dark Temptations" />

==Equipment==
Saylew wore dark-gray [[Robe/Legends|robes]] like many Pilgrims and carried a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]].<ref name="Dark Temptations" />

==Behind the scenes==
Saylew first appeared in the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]]-class mission "High-Tech Savages" in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] released by [[BioWare]] in [[2011]]. He later reappears in the mission "Dark Temptations," in which the player can choose to either kill the villagers for [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side]] points, fail to convince them to leave for [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-side]] points, or Force-persuade them to leave for maximum light-side points. As the Jedi Knight is a Republic character and is thus assumed to make choices that reward the maximum light-side points, this article assumes Saylew survived.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />
